value.body: Designs, installs and maintains heating, ventilation and air-conditioning systems for offices, malls, hospitals, data centres and factories. Employers include MEP consultancies, HVAC contractors, equipment manufacturers and facility-management firms. Depending on the role, the day goes on heat-load calculations and duct drawings, or on site supervising installation, testing and commissioning.

items.label: Typical entry
items.note: A mechanical or refrigeration diploma also leads to site and service roles

items.label: References used
items.value: ISHRAE and ASHRAE guidelines, National Building Code

items.label: ISHRAE membership
items.note: Indian Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Engineers; includes student members

items.label: UG enrolment, Mechanical Engineering
items.note: All mechanical students, of whom only some move into HVAC
items.source: AISHE 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), Table 12, actual responses

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join an HVAC contractor or MEP firm as a site or design trainee, or an equipment maker as a sales or service engineer. A short HVAC design course covering heat-load calculation and duct sizing is a common add-on. Student membership of ISHRAE gives access to workshops and industry contacts.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Equipment selection — chillers, AHUs, VRF systems

value.title: At a glance
items: Two main tracks: design (office-based) and execution or service (site-based).
Next roles: senior design engineer, project manager, or energy and green-building consulting.
Demand follows commercial construction and data-centre building.

value.title: Undergraduate enrolment in Mechanical Engineering
value.note: Based on institutions that responded to AISHE each year; the entry degree for most HVAC engineers, not a count of HVAC jobs.
